## Data

```{python}
df = pd.read_csv("data_for_drivers_analysis.csv")
drivers = ['trust','build','differs','easy','appealing','rewarding','popular','service','impact']
LABELS = {
    'trust':'Trust','build':'Build Quality','differs':'Differentiated',
    'easy':'Easy to Use','appealing':'Appealing','rewarding':'Rewarding',
    'popular':'Popular','service':'Good Service','impact':'Makes Impact',
}
X = df[drivers].values
y = df['satisfaction'].values
print(f"N = {len(df):,} | Brands = {df['brand'].nunique()} | R² full model = ?")
```

## Method 1: Pearson Correlations

```{python}
pearson = df[drivers].corrwith(df['satisfaction'])
pearson_labeled = pearson.rename(index=LABELS).sort_values(ascending=False)
print(pearson_labeled.round(4).to_string())
```

## Method 2: Standardized Regression Coefficients

```{python}
X_s = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)
y_s = StandardScaler().fit_transform(y.reshape(-1,1)).ravel()
ols = sm.OLS(y_s, sm.add_constant(X_s)).fit()
std_betas = pd.Series(ols.params[1:], index=[LABELS[d] for d in drivers])
print(std_betas.sort_values(ascending=False).round(4).to_string())
print(f"\nFull model R² = {ols.rsquared:.4f}")
```

## Method 3: Drop-One R² (Usefulness)

```{python}
full_r2 = sm.OLS(y, sm.add_constant(X)).fit().rsquared
drop_one = {}
for i, col in enumerate(drivers):
    X_d = np.delete(X, i, axis=1)
    drop_one[LABELS[col]] = full_r2 - sm.OLS(y, sm.add_constant(X_d)).fit().rsquared
print(pd.Series(drop_one).sort_values(ascending=False).round(5).to_string())
```

## Method 4: Shapley Values (Custom Code, Linear Regression, R² value function)

```{python}
#| cache: true
def r2_cache_build(X, y):
    n = X.shape[1]
    cache = {}
    for size in range(n + 1):
        for subset in combinations(range(n), size):
            cache[subset] = (0.0 if len(subset) == 0
                             else sm.OLS(y, sm.add_constant(X[:, list(subset)])).fit().rsquared)
    return cache

def shapley_linear(X, y, names):
    n = len(names)
    cache = r2_cache_build(X, y)
    sv = {}
    for j in range(n):
        others = [i for i in range(n) if i != j]
        s = 0.0
        for size in range(n):
            for subset in combinations(others, size):
                w = math.factorial(size) * math.factorial(n-size-1) / math.factorial(n)
                s += w * (cache[tuple(sorted(subset+(j,)))] - cache[subset])
        sv[names[j]] = s
    return sv, cache

shapley_raw, cache = shapley_linear(X, y, drivers)
shapley_s = pd.Series({LABELS[k]: v for k, v in shapley_raw.items()}).sort_values(ascending=False)
print(shapley_s.round(4).to_string())
print(f"\nShapley sum = {sum(shapley_raw.values()):.6f} | R² = {cache[tuple(range(len(drivers)))]:.6f}")
```

## Method 5: Johnson's Relative Weights

```{python}
def johnsons_rw(X, y):
    Xs = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)
    ys = StandardScaler().fit_transform(y.reshape(-1,1)).ravel()
    p = Xs.shape[1]
    Rxx = np.corrcoef(Xs.T)
    rxy = np.array([np.corrcoef(Xs[:,j], ys)[0,1] for j in range(p)])
    eigvals, V = np.linalg.eigh(Rxx)
    eigvals = np.maximum(eigvals, 1e-10)
    beta_ols = np.linalg.lstsq(Rxx, rxy, rcond=None)[0]
    beta_z = V.T @ beta_ols
    rw = np.array([
        sum((V[j,k]*np.sqrt(eigvals[k]))**2 * beta_z[k]**2 for k in range(p))
        for j in range(p)
    ])
    return rw, float(rxy @ beta_ols)

rw, R2_jrw = johnsons_rw(X, y)
johnson_s = pd.Series(rw, index=[LABELS[d] for d in drivers]).sort_values(ascending=False)
print(johnson_s.round(4).to_string())
print(f"\nJohnson sum = {rw.sum():.6f} | R² = {R2_jrw:.6f}")
```

## Method 6: Random Forest -- Mean Decrease in Gini

```{python}
rf = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=1000, random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
rf.fit(X, y)
gini = pd.Series(rf.feature_importances_, index=[LABELS[d] for d in drivers]).sort_values(ascending=False)
print(gini.round(4).to_string())
```

## Bonus: Shapley Values for Logistic Regression (GLM, McFadden pseudo-R²)

```{python}
#| cache: true
y_bin = (df['satisfaction'] >= 4).astype(int).values

def mcfadden_r2(X_sub, y_bin):
    if X_sub.shape[1] == 0:
        return 0.0
    clf = LogisticRegression(max_iter=500, solver='lbfgs', C=1e6)
    clf.fit(X_sub, y_bin)
    p = np.clip(clf.predict_proba(X_sub)[:,1], 1e-9, 1-1e-9)
    ll_m = np.sum(y_bin*np.log(p) + (1-y_bin)*np.log(1-p))
    p0 = y_bin.mean()
    ll_0 = len(y_bin)*(p0*np.log(p0) + (1-p0)*np.log(1-p0))
    return 1.0 - ll_m / ll_0

def shapley_glm(X, y_bin, names, val_fn):
    n = len(names)
    vc = {}
    for size in range(n+1):
        for subset in combinations(range(n), size):
            vc[subset] = val_fn(X[:, list(subset)], y_bin) if subset else 0.0
    sv = {}
    for j in range(n):
        others = [i for i in range(n) if i != j]
        s = 0.0
        for size in range(n):
            for subset in combinations(others, size):
                w = math.factorial(size)*math.factorial(n-size-1)/math.factorial(n)
                s += w*(vc[tuple(sorted(subset+(j,)))]-vc[subset])
        sv[names[j]] = s
    return sv, vc

shapley_glm_raw, glm_cache = shapley_glm(X, y_bin, drivers, mcfadden_r2)
glm_s = pd.Series({LABELS[k]: v for k, v in shapley_glm_raw.items()}).sort_values(ascending=False)
print(glm_s.round(4).to_string())
print(f"\nGLM Shapley sum = {sum(shapley_glm_raw.values()):.6f}")
print(f"Full McFadden R² = {glm_cache[tuple(range(len(drivers)))]:.6f}")
```

## Full Comparison Table

```{python}
results = pd.DataFrame({
    'Pearson r':   pearson.rename(index=LABELS),
    'Std. Beta':   pd.Series(ols.params[1:], index=[LABELS[d] for d in drivers]),
    'Drop-one R²': pd.Series(drop_one),
    'Shapley':     pd.Series({LABELS[k]:v for k,v in shapley_raw.items()}),
    "Johnson's RW":pd.Series(rw, index=[LABELS[d] for d in drivers]),
    'RF Gini':     gini,
})
results_norm = (results / results.sum()) * 100
results_norm = results_norm.sort_values('Shapley', ascending=False)

def color_cell(val):
    if val >= 20:    return "background-color: #dcfce7; color: #166534; font-weight:600"
    elif val >= 14:  return "background-color: #fef9c3; color: #854d0e"
    elif val <= 6:   return "background-color: #fee2e2; color: #991b1b"
    return ""

display(
    results_norm.round(1).style
    .applymap(color_cell)
    .format("{:.1f}%")
    .set_table_styles([
        {"selector":"thead th","props":[("background-color",NAVY),("color","white"),
             ("font-weight","600"),("padding","0.45rem 0.9rem"),("text-align","center")]},
        {"selector":"tbody td","props":[("padding","0.4rem 0.9rem"),("text-align","center")]},
        {"selector":"tbody th","props":[("font-weight","500"),("padding","0.4rem 0.9rem"),
             ("text-align","left"),("background-color","#f8fafc")]},
        {"selector":"table","props":[("border-collapse","collapse"),("width","100%"),
             ("margin","1rem 0"),("font-size","0.88em")]},
    ])
    .set_caption("Normalized importance scores (% of column total). Green = top, yellow = middle, red = bottom.")
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-heatmap
z_vals = results_norm.values
fig = go.Figure(go.Heatmap(
    z=z_vals,
    x=results_norm.columns.tolist(),
    y=results_norm.index.tolist(),
    colorscale=[[0,"#fee2e2"],[0.5,"#fef9c3"],[1,"#dcfce7"]],
    text=[[f"{v:.1f}%" for v in row] for row in z_vals],
    texttemplate="%{text}",
    textfont=dict(size=11),
    colorbar=dict(title="% of total"),
    zmin=0, zmax=25,
))
fig.update_layout(
    title="Key drivers heatmap: normalized importance by method",
    height=420, paper_bgcolor="white",
    font=dict(family="Arial", size=12),
    margin=dict(l=140, r=30, t=60, b=80),
)
show(fig)
```
